Concrete resurfacing in Melbourne

Resurfacing, or just a very good clean?

Resurfacing means bonding a new layer over the slab you have. It works, it looks excellent, and a large share of the driveways quoted for it in Melbourne never needed it. Before anyone pours anything, it is worth knowing which of three jobs yours actually is.

  • A concreting trade, not a cleaning one
  • We do the clean and the seal
  • Assessed before anything is committed
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Services
  3. Sealing and surface protection
  4. Concrete resurfacing

Where we stand on this

Resurfacing is concreting work. Laying a bonded overlay or a spray on topping is a different trade with different licensing, and Prime Exteriors does not do it. Anyone telling you otherwise on an exterior cleaning website is selling you something.

What we do is everything either side of it. We will tell you honestly whether the slab needs an overlay at all, because we have no reason to sell you one. If it does, you need a concreter and we will say so. If it does not, which is more often than the industry lets on, a clean and a seal or a colour seal gets most of the result for a fraction of the cost and a fraction of the disruption.

The decision

Five things a slab does, and the answer to each

Walk the slab and find which row it is in. Most driveways in Melbourne are in one of the first three.

What the slab is doing, and which answer it takes.
  What is really happening What it takes
Grey, dull and stained Surface contamination. Road film, oil, tannin from a gum, and years of it A clean. The concrete underneath is sound and usually comes up far better than people expect. Concrete cleaning
Clean but patchy and tired The cement paste has weathered off the top, exposing uneven sand and stone. The slab is fine, the look is not A clean, then a colour seal, which evens the tone and puts a finish back on it
Dusting and absorbing everything An unsealed or long unsealed slab. Every spill goes in because there is nothing on top of it A clean, then a penetrating or topical sealer. The dusting stops and the next spill sits on the surface
Spalling, flaking or pitted The top few millimetres are breaking away, usually from reinforcement rusting, salt, or a bad original pour This is the resurfacing case. A concreter, not a cleaner. Cleaning it will take more of it off, and sealing it only seals in the failure
Cracked through, lifting or moving A structural problem under the slab: tree roots, subsidence, inadequate reinforcement Neither of the above. An overlay over a moving slab cracks again within a season. This needs a concreter to look at what is underneath it

Swipe for the rest of the columns

What an overlay actually involves

The part the quote does not mention

The slab is out of action for days

Preparation, the pour and the cure. On a single driveway that is realistically three to five days of not parking on it, in weather that cooperates.

The levels change

An overlay adds height. Where a driveway meets a garage threshold, a door sweep or a drainage grate, somebody has to have thought about that beforehand.

It inherits the slab below it

An overlay is bonded to what is already there. If the slab moves, the overlay cracks in the same place. Fixing the cause comes first, always.

It is the most expensive of the three

By a wide margin, and that is before the disruption. Which is exactly why it is worth knowing whether a clean and a seal would have done.

What we will do

Three things, and one thing we will not

In scope

The work either side of a resurfacing decision.

  • Assessing the slab and telling you which of the five rows above it is in
  • Cleaning the slab back so the real condition is visible rather than guessed at
  • Sealing, colour sealing or anti slip sealing once it is clean and dry
  • Preparing and cleaning a slab before a concreter overlays it, if that is the answer
  • Cleaning and resealing an existing overlay that has gone dull

Not in scope

Different trade, different licence.

  • Laying a bonded overlay, a spray on topping or a stencil finish
  • Grinding, cutting or making good a structural crack
  • Replacing a slab or any part of one
  • Anything that changes the level or the fall of a surface

Questions

Before anybody pours anything

How do I know if my driveway needs resurfacing?

Run your hand over it. If it is simply discoloured, it needs cleaning. If the top surface comes away as grit on your palm, or you can see flakes lifting, that is spalling and it is the resurfacing case.

Send a photo and a close up and you will get a straight answer. We do not sell overlays, so there is nothing in it for us either way.

Can you clean a slab that is already spalling?

We would rather not. Pressure on a surface that is already letting go takes more of it off, and then the problem looks worse and is blamed on the clean.

Where only a small area is affected and the rest is sound, there is sometimes a sensible middle path. That is a judgement made on the slab, not from a web page.

Is colour sealing the same as resurfacing?

No, and the two get confused constantly because both change how a slab looks. A colour seal is a coating that goes on top of the existing surface and follows every contour of it. Resurfacing adds a new layer of material and can change the texture entirely.

A colour seal costs a fraction as much and is reversible in the sense that it wears rather than has to be removed. Concrete colour sealing.

Will sealing stop a slab from spalling further?

Not reliably, and a topical sealer over an actively spalling slab can trap moisture under the coating and make it worse. If the cause is reinforcement corroding or salt, the sealer is treating a symptom.

On a sound slab, sealing is genuinely preventive. That is the difference.

Do you work with concreters?

We will tell you plainly when you need one and what to ask them. The preparation work, cleaning the slab back so the overlay bonds to concrete rather than to oil and road film, is work we do and it is worth doing properly.

We do not take a referral fee, which is why the advice about whether you need one at all is worth something.
